clue.text: Sort of tracks — seen in the garden?

definitions.meaning: the continuous linked tracks on tanks and bulldozers are named after a crawling larva
a leaf-munching larva that turns into a butterfly or moth

explanation.surface: Someone puzzles over what kind of tracks have appeared among the garden beds.
explanation.definitionFit: Tank treads are called after the many-legged larva, which is also a familiar garden pest.

clue.text: Upset? Depends how big-headed one is!

definitions.meaning: the measurement of one's hat depends on the head's girth

explanation.surface: Whether someone gets upset depends on how conceited they are.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that overturns tips over; split, the word is the measure of one's headwear.

clue.text: Seabirds wheel around the stern

indicators.note: the letters turn about into a new order

explanation.surface: Gulls circle the back of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Terns are slender sea birds related to gulls.

clue.text: Reserve having to practise while the others go out

indicators.note: the others stand on the outside, around the practice word

parts.note: the rest means everyone else
to train is to practise

explanation.surface: A reserve player must keep training while the rest of the team head out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go out' puts REST on the outside of TRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve and restraint both mean holding back one's feelings.

clue.text: One gets no thanks for this small item

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
no means nothing, zero, the letter O
ta is an informal British word for thanks

explanation.surface: A small item goes unthanked.
explanation.definitionFit: An iota, from a tiny Greek letter, means a very small amount.

clue.text: Final position held, call in the army

parts.note: last means final
a post is a job or position someone holds

explanation.surface: A soldier holds the final position as a bugle sounds in the army.
explanation.definitionFit: This bugle call ends the day in British forces and is played at military funerals.

clue.text: Wine and port provided with German agreement

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port
ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: Wine and port are served after a German says yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a Spanish red wine region and its wine.

clue.text: Regularly late? Yet sounding chivalrous

indicators.note: the word for chivalrous is pronounced like the answer

parts.note: knightly means chivalrous, like a knight

explanation.surface: A man who is always late still manages to sound gallant.
explanation.walkthrough: The K of KNIGHTLY is silent, so it is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done every night happens on a regular basis late in the day.

clue.text: Party policy won't be one's main interest

definitions.note: a noun phrase is implied: what something is when it is not your chief pursuit

parts.note: a side is a party in a dispute
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A politician says party policy will not be the main thing on their mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary pursuit kept beside one's chief occupation is a subsidiary activity.

clue.text: They have their supporters — hosts of them!

definitions.text: They have their supporters — hosts of them!

parts.words: They have their supporters — hosts of them!
parts.note: reads like a popular figure with crowds of fans, but the supporters are host animals or plants that feed freeloading organisms

explanation.surface: A celebrity is said to have whole crowds of supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: Freeloading organisms live off a host, which in effect supports them; 'hosts' is the biological term.

clue.text: Outstanding result of love taking wing

indicators.note: the first piece takes the second on after it, so they join side by side

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird in love takes to the air, a remarkable outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt still outstanding is one still due to be paid.

clue.text: Take cover

parts.note: reads as diving for shelter, but means taking out a policy that covers you against loss

explanation.definitionFit: Insurance is commonly called cover, so to buy a policy is to take cover.

clue.text: When father returned by himself the rift was obvious

indicators.note: the next piece is placed beside the reversed one
the word for father is written backwards, as if coming back

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
the father himself, so pa again, this time forwards
a rent is a tear or split

explanation.surface: When Dad came home on his own, the family split was plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns PA into AP; 'himself' refers back to father, giving PA again.
explanation.definitionFit: Something plainly evident is clearly visible to all.

clue.text: Miracle drug for backside in trouble

annotationWithheld.why: Miracle drug for backside in trouble: the parse is XI (side) inside RILE (trouble), all reversed, with 'back' fused into 'backside' so one word is both the reversal indicator and the fodder for XI
annotationWithheld.clue: Miracle drug for backside in trouble

clue.text: At sea no rating is lacking in knowledge

indicators.note: being at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sailor of no rank is clueless about the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' rearranges NO RATING; a rating is a naval sailor below officer rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without education or information is uninformed.

clue.text: In a way it repays harshness

indicators.note: in a different way, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone notes that harshness pays off, after a fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a way' rearranges IT REPAYS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Asperity is roughness or severity of manner, so a synonym for harshness.

clue.text: How the heat can knock one out

definitions.text: How the heat can knock one out

parts.words: How the heat can knock one out
parts.note: reads as hot weather making someone faint, but a heat is a qualifying race that removes losers from a competition

explanation.surface: Blazing weather can make someone pass out.
explanation.definitionFit: A preliminary round of a contest knocks out the losers, dropping them from the event.

clue.text: It's not in your cellar but could be in mine

definitions.text: It's not in your cellar but could be in mine

parts.words: It's not in your cellar but could be in mine
parts.note: sounds like one person's wine store against another's, but a cellar is a table condiment pot and a mine is a pit where the mineral is dug

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that something absent from your cellar may be found in theirs.
explanation.definitionFit: Halite is the mineral form of table seasoning, dug from underground workings rather than kept in a shaker.

clue.text: Gift from people backing party

indicators.note: the people come behind the party, so that word follows it

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A donation comes from voters supporting a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is a present of money or goods, a kind of gift.

clue.text: Young socialite gets lace torn in bad fall

parts.note: a deb is a debutante, a young woman entering high society

indicators.note: the lace is ripped up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A debutante tears her lace dress in a nasty tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden collapse or humiliating failure.

clue.text: Manage to show the way

definitions.meaning: to run or be in charge of something
to point someone along the right route

explanation.surface: A boss is told to manage by showing the way.
explanation.definitionFit: One verb covers both running an operation and giving someone route guidance.

clue.text: He can just about stand up for himself

definitions.text: He can just about stand up for himself

parts.words: He can just about stand up for himself
parts.note: reads as someone barely able to defend himself, but literally a small child only just able to stand upright unaided

explanation.surface: A timid man can barely defend himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A child learning to walk can barely keep upright on its own.

clue.text: Private quarters

parts.note: reads as personal rooms, but a private is a soldier and these are a soldier's living quarters

explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers, including privates, are housed in military accommodation blocks.

clue.text: Get involved with an intermediary

indicators.note: the letters are tangled together into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to get involved with a go-between.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent acts on another's behalf as a go-between.

clue.text: Describing Jill when cut off by Edward

definitions.text: Describing Jill when cut off by Edward

indicators.note: the next piece is set beside the shortened name
the last letter of the name is chopped away

parts.note: taken as written
Ted is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Jill has been dumped by her boyfriend Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut off' drops the last letter of the name. Read as a whole, the clue describes how Jill feels when her boyfriend Edward leaves her, so it is both definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman dropped by her lover has been abandoned, which is what the word describes.

clue.text: Drunk in snug

explanation.surface: Someone is drunk in the cosy back room of a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for intoxicated, and also describing clothes that fit closely.

clue.text: A small credit note on which little can be raised

definitions.text: on which little can be raised
definitions.note: a noun is meant: a plot of ground able to grow only a small crop

parts.note: CR is the short form of credit
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A small loan note will raise only a little money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' suggests money, but here means crops grown on a small field.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of land area is a small plot, on which crops can be grown.

clue.text: Thrash about the ring showing little craft

indicators.note: the beating word goes around the ring

parts.note: to cane is to beat with a stick
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone flails about in the boxing ring, a sign of little skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe is a small boat, so a little vessel.

clue.text: Chilled port for Michael?

definitions.meaning: a cold northern Russian port on the White Sea
Saint Michael is one of the chief angels

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether Michael would like a glass of chilled port.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkhangelsk, an icy Russian harbour, has this English name, which is also the rank of Saint Michael among angels.

clue.text: Exactly how rent should be paid

definitions.meaning: rent goes to the person who lets the property, the landlord

explanation.surface: Tenants are reminded exactly how the rent must be paid.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means precisely; whimsically, a landlord who lets property is one who receives the rent.
